paragraphs: Born in Camden to Nigerian parents, Okonkwo joined Arsenal's academy at eight and rose through their youth ranks. He went out on development loans to sharpen his game — Crewe Alexandra, where he made his professional debut, then Austrian Bundesliga side Sturm Graz — before a breakthrough season-long loan to Wrexham in 2023–24, replacing the retired Ben Foster. He made 40 appearances across all competitions with 16 clean sheets, helping the club reach League One as National League runners-up. Wrexham made the move permanent on a free transfer in June 2024, and Okonkwo switched international allegiance to Nigeria in April 2026.

Mason grew up in Sheffield in the long shadow of his father Dave's gloves — Dave Webber kept goal for Sheffield United's reserves before a knee injury ended his career at 24. Mason joined Sheffield Wednesday's Academy at 8, was released at 12, and spent two seasons at Stocksbridge Park Steels' youth setup before a regional goalkeeping showcase in Manchester put him on Wrexham's radar. Jenkins' staff identified his raw reflexes as the standout attribute in a group of 40 trialists. He arrived in Wrexham in June 2025 as the quietest player in the dorms and, by most accounts, still is. Promoted to the first team on 21 March 2026 as emergency backup goalkeeper following Arthur Okonkwo's training-ground injury, he made his senior debut at Bramall Lane — the ground his father once played in front of for Sheffield United's reserves — and was later Man of the Match keeping a clean sheet in the Youth Academy Rush Tournament final before his senior league debut against Hull City.

Signed from Burnley on transfer deadline day 2026-08-31 (£6.2m) as senior cover and eventual competition behind Arthur Okonkwo. A Dutch goalkeeper known for his kicking range (84) more than his shot-stopping reflexes at this stage.

Nico grew up a five-minute walk from the Volksparkstadion in Hamburg, following HSV's reserve side with his father Lukas before joining their goalkeeping academy at 8 and being released at 15. Wrexham's German scout Klaus Weidmann signed him in a regional trial sweep in August 2025. Promoted to the first team on 13 January 2027, both Long Ball Pass and Cross Claimer already live on the PlayStyles tab for the towering 6'7" sweeper-keeper prospect.

Amelia is a full Curaçao international right-back, part of a national team that has climbed rapidly up the FIFA rankings this decade. Born in Willemstad, he moved to the Netherlands as a teenager to join FC Dordrecht's academy, breaking into their first team in the Eerste Divisie before a step up to Almere City sharpened his overlapping runs and delivery from wide areas. He earned his senior Curaçao debut in a CONCACAF Nations League qualifier and has since become a regular fixture in the squad. Wrexham identified him during a scouting trip through the Dutch second tier and signed him in 2025 as competition and eventual succession at right-back.
Curaçao international status confirmed; club career details below are a plausible reconstruction rather than sourced record, as no public playing history could be found for this name.
Italian right-back, 17, signed as a free agent, willing to negotiate new terms. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.
Dutch right-back, 20, signed from Sunderland for a reported $3.7m. Willing to negotiate new terms. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.

Born in Wellington, Cacace began with Wellington Phoenix in the A-League before moving to Europe in 2020 with Belgian side Sint-Truiden, then a loan-to-buy switch to Serie A club Empoli in 2022. Across four seasons in Italy he made over 80 appearances, establishing himself as a reliable, attack-minded left-back. He is a mainstay of the New Zealand national team with over 30 caps, captaining the All Whites to the 2024 OFC Nations Cup title and being named the tournament's MVP. He joined newly-promoted Wrexham in July 2025 for a club-record fee.

A left-footed centre-back from Manchester City's academy, Doyle captained their youth sides before a series of high-profile Championship loans built his reputation as one of England's top defensive prospects — Sunderland (League One promotion), Coventry City (play-off final defeat on penalties), Leicester City (automatic promotion to the Premier League), and Norwich City. He represented England at U19 level, scoring in the final as England won the 2022 UEFA European U19 Championship. Doyle signed permanently for Wrexham on a four-year deal in August 2025 and was named to the EFL Championship Team of the Season in his first year.

A boyhood Wrexham fan from Frodsham, Cleworth previously played for Connah's Quay Nomads' youth setup before joining Wrexham's own academy at 12 in 2014. He made his senior debut aged 17 in September 2019, with a brief loan to Cymru Premier side Caernarfon Town in 2020–21 giving him senior men's experience. Cleworth has been ever-present through the club's run of three consecutive promotions, developing from a defensive stalwart into a genuine goal threat — a three-time Young Player of the Season and Wrexham's Players' Player of the Season for 2024–25.
Entire senior career has been at Wrexham — no meaningful "prior club" history exists to report beyond a single loan spell.
English centre-back, 19, signed from Manchester United for a reported $18.4m. Willing to negotiate new terms. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.
Spanish centre-back, 19, signed from Barcelona for $1.9m. Not willing to negotiate new terms. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.

Jermaine grew up in Blacon, Chester, close enough to the Racecourse to see the floodlights from his estate. Released by Chester FC's academy at 14, he was spotted at a Colliers Park trial day by Wrexham youth coordinator Rhys Davies. Promoted to the first team on 13 January 2027 — now goes by Jermaine rather than the Jamie tag he carried through the academy.

Vittorio grew up in Florence's Oltrarno district, starting at Fiorentina's academy at 9 before being released at 14. Wrexham's Italian scout Gianluca Ferrara flagged him in a Tuscan youth league match, rating his ceiling among the highest in the academy group. Promoted to the first team on 13 January 2027.

Bobadilla is a Paraguayan midfielder who came through Cerro Porteño's academy in Asunción, making his professional debut in the 2021 Copa Libertadores. His performances for La Academia earned a move to Brazilian giants São Paulo FC in December 2023 for a reported $3m fee, and his form there was strong enough to put him in Paraguay's picture for the 2026 World Cup squad. In this save, his path diverges from there — Wrexham's scouting network identified him as a free-agent target in early 2026, and he signed with the club, making an immediate impact with a debut goal against Millwall on his first appearance. Known for his passing range, tackling, and Long Ball Pass playstyle, he slots in as a ball-winning presence in central midfield.

Cerro Porteño academy background, São Paulo FC transfer, and Paraguay international recognition are all real and confirmed. His actual real-world career remained at São Paulo through 2025–26 rather than moving to Wrexham as a free agent — that part is this save's simulation. Season-by-season apps/goals for his real career aren't included here since they weren't reliably sourced.

A US-born attacking midfielder of Mexican descent, Gutiérrez joined Chicago Fire's academy in 2015 and signed as a Homegrown Player in 2020. He developed into one of MLS's most creative young playmakers, topping 30+ appearances annually from 2022 onward and culminating in 11 goals in 2025.

Real career confirmed through Chicago Fire FC. His actual real-world move in this window was a reported $5m transfer to Liga MX side Guadalajara (Chivas) in December 2025 — no real transfer to Wrexham exists. FC26 licenses his stats/likeness, but the Wrexham move is a career-mode simulation, not something that happened in reality.

Santiago grew up in the Echesortu neighbourhood of Rosario — the same city that produced Lionel Messi and Gabriel Batistuta, a fact his father Rodrigo mentions in roughly four of every five conversations. He joined Newell's Old Boys' famous La Lepra youth system at age 8, spending six years in the academy that shaped so many Argentine greats. A Wrexham scout on a separate Buenos Aires assignment was tipped off about a left-footed winger from Rosario "with something special" and made the trip north. His signing was one of the longest negotiations in Wrexham's academy history — Rodrigo needed three video calls with Jenkins before agreeing that Wales was a better destination than River Plate's reserve setup. Promoted to the first team on 29 March 2026, he made his senior debut against Hull City with an assist on Keillor-Dunn's winner, capping a run in which he'd already fired the academy to Youth Academy Rush Tournament glory.

Juan Cruz grew up among vineyards in Mendoza's Luján de Cuyo region, where his father Hernán runs a small bodega producing Malbec wines he describes as "nothing special, but perfectly honest." He was the standout player in Mendoza's regional youth structure before being picked up by Talleres de Córdoba's academy at 13, then spotted by Wrexham scout Alejandro Ruiz during a session with San Lorenzo de Almagro's youth setup. He carries the highest potential ceiling in the entire squad (90–94), and Jenkins has been careful not to oversell him to the board even as the pressure to play him mounts. Promoted to the first team on 8 November 2026, with Jenkins telling reporters: "This kid has the potential to be special — I want him getting minutes with the first team now."

A Hungarian central midfielder born in Nyíregyháza, Vitális came through Győri ETO's academy and made his professional debut there in 2019. Since 2022 he has been with DAC 1904 Dunajská Streda in Slovakia, with loan spells back at Győr along the way, developing into a reliable box-to-box presence.

Real career confirmed through DAC Dunajská Streda/Győri ETO. No real transfer to Wrexham exists — FC26 licenses his stats/likeness, but the Wrexham move is a career-mode simulation. PlayStyles tab not yet screenshotted for this session.

Spanish CM/CDM/CAM, 19, signed from Real Madrid on 2026-12-29 for CM depth. An Exciting Prospect. Not willing to negotiate new terms. Wage $52K/w, market value $8.5m. Roles: Deep-Lying Playmaker+/Box-to-Box+/Playmaker+ (CM); Deep-Lying Playmaker+ (CDM); Half-Winger/Shadow Striker/Classic 10 (CAM). No PlayStyles confirmed yet. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.
Signed from Ajax for a reported £8.7m, an 18-year-old DR Congo midfielder. Not willing to negotiate new contract terms currently. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.
Tunisian defensive midfielder, 17, signed as a free agent, willing to negotiate new terms. Being converted from CDM to CB. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.

Emiliano grew up in Milan's Porta Romana neighbourhood with an Inter Milan ultras flag on his bedroom wall and an AC Milan youth academy badge on his training kit — a contradiction his father Roberto has never fully made peace with. He spent six years in AC Milan's youth setup before a spell at Atalanta's Bergamo academy, then joined Wrexham's August 2025 intake. Promoted to the first team on 27 December 2026 alongside academy teammate Marco Soria.

Spanish CM/CDM prospect, 17, signed from Villarreal 2026-08-31 (£2.0m) and immediately loaned to Swansea City for 12 months to gain first-team minutes (70/30 wage split, Wrexham pays 30%). Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.
English winger, 17, product of Liverpool's academy known for pace and direct dribbling out wide. Real-world detailed career history not yet confirmed for this save.
Slovak winger, 20, signed from Athletic Bilbao for $22.1m on 2026-08-15. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.

Marco grew up in Córdoba, Argentina's second city, where his father Ramón drove a bus route that happened to pass Talleres' training ground twice a day — close enough that Marco talked his way into a trial at 11 and stayed in the academy until an ACL tear at 17 cost him a full year of development. Wrexham's South American scout Diego Aranda signed him in March 2026. Promoted to the first team on 27 December 2026 and made his senior debut off the bench two days later at Ipswich Town.

No real-world footballer named Yacel Amrizi could be found in any public football database or news source. This appears to be a fictional/EA-generated depth player rather than a real licensed pro. No bio or career history is published here rather than fabricate one.

A Colombian winger, Gómez broke through at Millonarios, scoring 9 goals in 49 appearances and helping the club win the 2022 Copa Colombia. That form earned a January 2023 move to MLS side Real Salt Lake, where he was a key attacking outlet (14 goals, 16 assists in 56 games) and earned his senior Colombia debut. In August 2024 he stepped up to Ligue 1 with Rennes.

Real career confirmed through Real Salt Lake/Rennes. His actual real-world move in this window was to Brazilian club Vasco da Gama (signed through Jan 2031) — no real transfer to Wrexham exists. FC26 licenses his stats/likeness, but the Wrexham move is a career-mode simulation, not something that happened in reality.

The son of former Everton/Fulham forward Danny Cadamarteri, Bailey joined Sheffield Wednesday's academy at eight and made his first-team debut in November 2023. A loan at Lincoln City in 2024–25 saw him get regular senior minutes, scoring 8 goals and sharpening his finishing. Back at Hillsborough for 2025–26 he made 30 appearances before a deadline-day move to Wrexham on a contract to 2029 in February 2026. Eligible for Jamaica internationally, he's regarded as a promising young forward still developing his end product at Championship level.
Real academy is Sheffield Wednesday, not Wrexham — he arrived via a first-team transfer in Feb 2026, not academy promotion.

A Ukrainian winger born in Kyiv, Veleten came through Dynamo Kyiv's academy and is now with Polissya Zhytomyr, who signed him in August 2025 on a contract through 2029. He has earned senior caps for Ukraine. Away from the pitch, he served in Ukraine's Territorial Defence Forces during the 2022 Russian invasion, including roughly two months at the front near Kramatorsk.

Real career confirmed through Dynamo Kyiv/Polissya Zhytomyr. No real transfer to Wrexham exists — FC26 licenses his stats/likeness, but the Wrexham move is a career-mode simulation. PlayStyles tab not yet screenshotted for this session.

An Ecuadorian forward born in Esmeraldas, Minda rose through Independiente del Valle's academy, winning five titles including the Ecuadorian Serie A (2021) and Copa Sudamericana (2022), before a January 2025 move to Brazilian giants Clube Atlético Mineiro. He has been capped for Ecuador at the 2024 Copa América and named to the 2026 World Cup squad.

Real career confirmed through Independiente del Valle/Atlético Mineiro. No real transfer to Wrexham exists — FC26 licenses his stats/likeness, but the Wrexham move is a career-mode simulation. Financial tab (contract/wage/value) not yet screenshotted for this session.

Signed straight from Manchester United's academy as an eighteen-year-old striker prospect, contract accepted with no negotiation friction. Full real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save — treat as a fresh academy graduate rather than an established name.
Croatian forward, 25, signed as a free agent, willing to negotiate new terms. PlayStyles: Dead Ball, Incisive Pass, Long Ball Pass. Real-world career detail not yet confirmed for this save.

Sandoval grew up three streets from Boca Juniors' Casa Amarilla in La Boca, and his earliest football memory is being lifted onto his uncle's shoulders inside La Bombonera for a Superclásico he was really too young to remember clearly — he swears he does anyway. He joined Boca's own academy at seven, a left-footed No. 10 who could thread a pass through spaces that didn't look like they existed, and stayed until fifteen, when a coaching change upstream tightened the pathway to the first team and his family made the harder call: better development minutes somewhere else than a bench seat at the biggest club in Argentina. A trial arranged through a former Boca youth-team physio who'd relocated to Wales brought him to Colliers Park at sixteen, and homesickness nearly won in the first month — he still calls his grandmother in La Boca every single Sunday without fail. What kept him there was simple: nobody in Wrexham's academy had ever asked him to stop trying the pass that only works one time in five. Two years on, it's starting to work more than one time in five.

Faure was born in Nantes and spent his whole childhood a ten-minute walk from the Stade de la Beaujoire, close enough that on European nights the crowd noise used to drift over the rooftops into his bedroom. He joined FC Nantes' academy at eight and was considered one of the better wide players in his age group until a serious ankle injury at fourteen cost him the better part of a season — by the time he was fit again, the club had moved on to a younger intake and there was no path back. Wrexham's French scouting network, the same one that would later bring in Bertrand and Collin, picked him up on the recommendation of a Nantes youth coach who'd stayed in touch out of guilt as much as belief. He signed without ever having watched a full Wrexham match, on the strength of one phone call and a highlight reel. His father, a dockworker at the Port of Nantes, has since become fluent in reading a Welsh football form guide he cannot pronounce a word of, purely so he has something to argue about with his son over video calls.

Brunel grew up in Lille's Vieux-Lille district in a family with no real football pedigree — his mother ran a bakery, his father drove regional trains — and discovered the game almost by accident, filling in for a five-a-side team a cousin's friend needed one player short for. He was spotted at twelve playing street football in a car park near the Grand Place by a LOSC Lille academy scout doing nothing more official than picking up his own kid from practice, and spent four years in Lille's youth setup before a growth spurt that arrived a year later than his coaches had banked on cost him his place in the intake. Wrexham signed him at seventeen off a single trial week, mostly on the strength of a poacher's instinct inside the box that scouts kept describing as "older than his legs." He still helps out behind the counter at his mother's bakery every visit home, and swears the muscle memory of kneading dough for years is the real source of his shot power — nobody on the coaching staff has found a way to disprove it.

Tine's unlikely path to the Racecourse starts on a dirt pitch outside Port-Gentil, Gabon, where he was first noticed not by a scout but by a Wrexham content producer filming B-roll for a documentary about the club's global academy scouting trips — a fifteen-year-old outjumping and outmuscling boys three years older for every ball in a pickup match happening on the edge of the shoot. The footage got forwarded up the chain almost as a joke; nobody expected it to end with a signing. It did. Wrexham flew him to Wales for a two-week trial that turned into a four-year contract, and within his first month of first-team training, staff were already comparing his combination of raw power and finishing instinct to strikers a decade further into their careers. He arrives with almost no football pedigree on paper — no famous academy, no viral highlight reel before that one — and every bit of upside a club could hope to find for nothing. His signing bonus went straight into a savings account for his mother, who still runs a fish stall in Port-Gentil's central market and has not, as of this writing, agreed to stop.

Stephane grew up in Marseille's Le Panier district, where street football on cobbled, sloped alleys shaped a close, low center of gravity that coaches now point to as the source of his footwork. He joined Olympique de Marseille's academy at 9 and stayed until 14, when a philosophy shift toward taller, more physical wingers left him without a contract. Wrexham's French scout Marc Delacroix saw him at the same regional trial that produced Jules Collin, and both signed on 2026-08-15 in the window that also brought Germany's Nico Kopp. His five-star dribbling and a POT ceiling among the highest in the academy made him a name the coaching staff mentioned unprompted well before his sixteenth birthday, and the promotion to the senior squad — with an immediate loan to Carrarese Calcio to get first-team minutes his own dressing room couldn't offer yet — came with the club's 'Has Potential to be Special' scouting tag attached. His father Antoine, a dockworker at the Port of Marseille, has started rearranging his shift pattern around kickoff times in Italy instead of Wales.

Nathan grew up in Brest, on Brittany's Atlantic coast, in a family that has fished out of the same harbor for three generations — his father Yann still expected him to join the boats until a growth spurt at 14 made football the more obvious calling. He came through Stade Brestois' academy before being released at 15 when the club's recruitment turned toward physically bigger forwards from elsewhere in France. Wrexham's French scout Marc Delacroix found him at the same December 2026 regional showcase that produced Thierry Besse, and both signed on 2026-12-15. Genuinely comfortable off either foot — five stars each way, a rarity even at senior level — he was promoted to the first team and loaned straight to Barnet for two seasons to get the minutes a title-winning squad can't offer an eighteen-year-old yet. Yann has made peace with the football career, on one condition: Nathan still has to help haul nets whenever he's home.
